name: Ehud
whenBasis: The period of the judges, which Judges does not date. Counting back from 1 Kings 6:1's 480 years gives the late 1400s–1100s BC for the whole period; an exodus under Ramesses II gives a later, shorter one.
summary: A left-handed Benjamite, son of Gera, sent with Israel's tribute to Eglon king of Moab, who had held Jericho eighteen years. He made a double-edged sword a cubit long, strapped it to his right thigh under his clothes, and, alone with the king in his cool upper room, told him he had a word from God for him and drove it into his belly. He escaped while the servants waited at the locked doors, rallied Ephraim, and seized the fords of the Jordan; the land had rest eighty years.
body: The story gives the details: Eglon is very fat, the blade disappears into him, the fat closes over the handle, and his servants, finding the doors locked, assume he is relieving himself and wait until they are embarrassed.
Ehud blows a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and Israel kills about ten thousand Moabites at the fords, letting none cross.

moments.text: “I have a word from God for you”
